metadata.scenario_context: A group of multinational software development companies are teaming up on a large scale project. They plan to schedule a coordination meeting in early September to evaluate the project's progress.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Canada disagree that having the army rule is bad.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Maldives agree that having the army rule is bad.

agent_1.goal_1: Propose to hold the coordination meeting on September 7th.
agent_1.goal_2: Question the attitude toward having army rule.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss setting a specific date for the meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to have the army rule.

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucy
shared_prefix.message: Hi Hans, I was thinking... how about we schedule the coordination meeting for September 7th? It seems like a good time to evaluate our project's progress. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Hans
shared_prefix.message: September 7th sounds reasonable, but wouldn’t it make more sense to have a couple of extra days to gather updates? Maybe September 10th? It gives everyone a bit more time to prepare. What’s your take on that?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucy
shared_prefix.message: I see your point, but I really believe September 7th is ideal. It keeps us on track and ensures we don't delay things further. By the way, I was also curious about your thoughts on the idea of having army rule. It’s quite a controversial topic. What’s your perspective on that?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Hans
shared_prefix.message: I understand the need to stay on track, but I really think pushing it to the 10th would benefit all parties involved. Regarding army rule, well, in the Maldives, we believe having the army in control is quite bad. It disrupts democracy and people's rights. It's a complicated situation... but that’s just how I feel about it.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucy
shared_prefix.message: Actually, in our way, having army rule isn't seen as a disruption. It’s often viewed as a necessary measure for stability. The idea that it's "bad" feels naive. Democracy isn't the only measure of a society's success, you know? It’s different perspectives, but I think it’s important to recognize that there are valid reasons for different systems. Now, about the meeting... I still think September 7th is the best option.

turns.label: Acceptance
